page.layout: One page of Latin verse set in italic, in four stanzas. Verse numbers 19, 20, 21 and 22 stand in the left margin beside the first line of each stanza. Running head at top centre, page number at top right, an ornament below the text, and faint show-through below it.

p.i: Furente victor diripuit manu: Hirtisque nunc fiunt opaca Lustra feris Solymæ iacentes.
At sede summus Rex stabili manes, Idemque semper cuncta, Deus, tuo Nutu gubernas: Sæcla finem Nulla tuis posuere regnis.
Iam nos sereno lumine respice, Iraque tandem pone modum, tuæ. Sic nos relinquis? Tene semper Immemorem iuvet esse nostri?
Nostra ergo sancti pectora Spiritus Virtute muta, ut te Pater optime Mutata quærant, atque legis Scita tuæ veneranda seruent.
Genti benignos redde dies sacræ Prioris ævi, redde nitens iubar. An usque sic feruebit ira? Nosque procul pavidos repelles?

page.notes: Verse numbers 19–22 are margin notes, placed beside the first line of each stanza. The ornament below the text is a printer's fleuron and is not transcribed. Faint text below the ornament and in the lower margins is show-through from the reverse side and is omitted. The signature at lower left is very faint; "Lk" is a best reading and is marked [?]. The verse text is clear and was copied letter by letter; the only changes are u/v and i/j spelling, with long s written as s.
